transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 34 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Samir Khatri (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Cascade - Lead ML); Priya Nair (Cascade PM); Ethan Gomez (Cascade Infra)

Summary:
Quick review of last week's prefetch + prefix/KV cache tuning results. Samir walked through hit rate changes, cost delta, and a few anomalies on tail latency. Decision to run a longer 24h prefetch experiment across two cohorts and share raw CSVs. Action items and follow-up scheduled.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is the Cascade prefetch pilot sync, we have about 35 minutes. Samir's gonna run through the results from the last three days, then Jordan/Priya can give feedback and we'll decide next steps.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood SE): yeah thanks Maya. quick note, um a couple of caveats in the data, we had a restart on node 4 last night so I filtered that out, but overall - big headline - KV hit rate moved from ~18% baseline to about 46% average after the prefix canonicalization + prefetcher enable.
[00:34] Jordan (Cascade): whoa that's pretty big, is that 46% across all traffic or just the warmed cohort?
[00:42] Samir: that's warmed cohort A, warmed via nightly prefetch that pulls top 10k prefixes per cohort. the control cohort B stayed roughly at 19%. aggregated across both it's ~32%.
[00:58] Priya: can you remind me what counts as a prefix here? like are user ids or session ids being included? we saw some weird duplicates last week.
[01:08] Samir: good q - prefix is the prompt up to the first system delim basically user prompt normalized. we do lowercase, strip punctuation for the key. but we saw some noise from session-based tokens where frontend appended a timestamp which prevented reuse - Jordan fixed a filter to drop that token, so results improved.
[01:26] Jordan: yeah that was the main change on our side, we added a strip and hash step. there might still be some template variants where PGN and P-G-N show up differently so Samir suggested a small tokenizer normalization.
[01:40] Maya: quick interruption - is the cost per token impacted? i.e. does the caching reduce calls enough to move the cost needle?
[01:48] Samir: short answer yes. from our estimates token-inference calls fell ~27% in the warmed cohort, cost-per-session down ~21% when accounting for extra prefetch compute. so net savings, but it's workload dependent.
[02:05] Ethan (Cascade): can you unpack the prefetch compute? are we paying more to precompute and it outweighs savings sometimes?
[02:13] Samir: we run a small batch job during off-peak that computes KV entries for the top prefixes and pushes them to the cache; that costs GPU cycles but it's cheaper than repeated decoding for high-volume prefixes. if your prefix distribution is very long tail the ROI is less.
[02:29] Priya: do you have a way to predict ROI? like a cutoff where prefetch saves money?
[02:36] Samir: yes we use a simple model: if expected reuse * avg_tokens_saved > prefetch_cost then prefetch. i'll send the estimator in the spreadsheet.
[02:45] Maya: and how about latency, especially p99? we saw a note in the doc about a tail increase?
[02:52] Samir: right, there's an interesting outlier - p50 improved by ~8ms, p95 improved ~15ms, but p99 had a small bump ~12ms in one cluster during peak. looked like eviction storms when a large batch of new prefixes invalidated KV working set and caused synchronous fallback requests.
[03:12] Jordan: eviction storms, yeah we hit that when we rolled a big marketing event - many new prefixes. can we smooth evictions?
[03:20] Samir: a few options: 1) gradual prefetch ramp (throttle writes to cache), 2) prioritized TTLs for recently-used keys, 3) session affinity so hot-ish users stay on nodes with warmed cache. we demoed session affinity last week but didn't enable it for this run.
[03:36] Ethan: session affinity sounds heavy for infra. do you have metrics on how much it helps?
[03:43] Samir: in our internal tests affinity reduced p99 spikes by ~30% for bursty cohorts. cost tradeoff is slightly less even distribution of load.
[03:51] Priya: what about prefix deduping? could normalization reduce new unique prefixes?
[03:56] Samir: yes, canonicalization reduced uniques by ~12% in our sample; more aggressive normalization (stopword stripping, templating) could do more but risks changing semantics. Jordan -- you pushed some templating, right?
[04:07] Jordan: yeah we templated a few prompts and rotated user-specific metadata into separate fields, which helped. however there are cases where semantics depend on that metadata so we had to be careful.
[04:18] Maya: any security or data retention concerns from prefetching? like are we caching any PII?
[04:24] Samir: we mask and hash user identifiers before writing to the KV, and prefetch jobs respect redwood_privet policy - wait, sorry 'Privet' - I mean 'Private' policy we set for Cascade. we also keep audit logs and TTLs are configurable. I will attach the security snippet.
[04:43] Priya: good. Ethan will want to see KMS/HSM integration details - we logged that as a follow-up.
[04:50] Maya: noted. ok next, anomalies - Samir you mentioned an odd latency spike on day two?
[04:56] Samir: yes, around 03:00 UTC there was a spike in p99, looked correlated with a garbage collection on the coordinator and concurrent batch writes to cache. node 4 restart i mentioned before is part of that. i suspect write-lock contention on the cache metadata store.
[05:12] Ethan: what store are you using for metadata? is it ZK or etcd?
[05:17] Samir: it's a lightweight raft-backed metadata store - a custom module in Redwood's runtime. sometimes under heavy concurrent writes it serializes and causes write stalls. we have a patch to make writes more async, but it needs load testing.
[05:29] Jordan: is that patch risky? can we run it in staging?
[05:32] Samir: should be safe, it's opt-in. i can deploy to your staging next week.
[05:36] Priya: let's do that before we roll to prod.
[05:39] Maya: great. Samir, can you share the raw CSVs and the small notebook? Jordan wanted the raw keys to look for weird templates.
[05:47] Samir: yes, i already uploaded a trimmed dump to the sheet - link: drive.google.com/cascade-poc/benchmarks (note: placeholder). raw CSVs and notebook are in the 'prefetch-analysis' tab.
[05:58] Jordan: perfect, i'll look at the duplicates and flag weird ones.
[06:02] Ethan: also, curious about metric timing - is hit rate measured per request or per token?
[06:09] Samir: per request for the KV lookup path; we also have token-saved metric which is a better cost proxy. I'll add that to the sheet.
[06:16] Priya: what's your recommendation for cohort size? we tested top 10k prefixes, is that the right granularity?
[06:22] Samir: depends on traffic volume. for Cascade scale top 10k covers ~55% of warm traffic; you could try 20k for marginal gains but higher prefetch cost. hence we want a 24h test to see diminishing returns.
[06:34] Maya: ok about test design, Samir, you suggested two cohorts A/B - what's the plan?
[06:39] Samir: cohort A: nightly prefetch of top 10k, cohort B: control. both instrumented for token-saved and latency; we'll run 24h under normal production-like traffic and then swap seasonally. export raw traces with trace IDs.
[06:53] Jordan: swap seasonally? you mean roll the prefetch to cohort B afterwards?
[06:57] Samir: yeah to avoid cohort bias. also we'll try a smaller ramp-in to avoid eviction storms.
[07:04] Ethan: can Redwood's runtime do gradual TTL warming? like soft writes that don't evict?
[07:09] Samir: we have a 'soft-warm' mode where prefetch tags keys as warm and they adopt shorter TTL until fully warmed. that's what we want for the next run.
[07:18] Priya: any thing else in the data? cost anomalies?
[07:22] Samir: one oddity - an infrequent prompt pattern caused very long KV values which bloated memory and caused occasional OOMs in the worker. we've added value-size clipping and an eviction priority for large values.
[07:36] Jordan: that was from a debug prompt that included full stack traces, we removed that generator.
[07:41] Maya: good catch. ok can we talk about prompt reuse strategy? Priya you mentioned wanting more deterministic reuse across templates.
[07:48] Priya: yeah we have many templates that differ only in filler wording; we'd like Redwood to map them to a canonical template to increase reuse without breaking meaning.
[07:57] Samir: conceptually there are three levers: canonicalization (normalize whitespace, tokens), templating (replace variables with placeholders), and semantic hashing (embedding-based near dedupe). each has tradeoffs.
[08:09] Jordan: semantic hashing sounds expensive though.
[08:12] Samir: it's heavier but can be used as a second-pass for near duplicates. the runtime can fallback: exact key -> templated key -> semantic similarity. we haven't enabled the semantic stage in this pilot due to cost.
[08:25] Priya: how do we measure false merges? we don't want to return a prompt answer meant for a different variable set.
[08:31] Samir: that's the risk - so we add semantic threshold and log sample mismatches for manual review. we also keep an 'escape hatch' where high-entropy user fields bypass reuse.
[08:43] Ethan: sounds sensible. can you expose the threshold as a config so we can tune?
[08:47] Samir: yes it's an operator setting in the config UI, default 0.82 for cosine sim.
[08:52] Maya: good. any competitor notes? Priya mentioned Anthropic's approach in their blog?
[08:58] Priya: they talked about local context caching but it's not open-sourced fully, we compared notes - Redwood's batch prefetch and KV approach seems more flexible for our use case.
[09:09] Maya: ok, back to evictions - Samir you said you had a mitigation patch to reduce metadata write contention. timeline?
[09:15] Samir: i can stage the patch tomorrow and run a 12h load test against your staging cluster, expecting to have results by the 25th.
[09:23] Jordan: would be great to include the tail traces so we can see if p99 improves.
[09:27] Samir: will do.
[09:29] Priya: one more UX ask - can we get a per-route dashboard that shows prefix reuse rate and token-saved so our PMs can track?
[09:37] Maya: that's in roadmap but we can provide a temporary dashboard snapshot. Samir, can you export a per-route CSV?
[09:42] Samir: yes exporting per-route is easy, will add to the sheet.
[09:46] Ethan: on the infra side, what's your recommended instance footprint for production with prefetch enabled?
[09:52] Samir: roughly +15% GPU for prefetch worker if you keep prefetch during off-peak; peak inference nodes don't need extra GPUs unless you enable semantic hashing online.
[10:04] Jordan: semantics off-line might be fine, we can recompute candidate keys nightly.
[10:08] Maya: ok wrapping up, let's recap next steps - Samir run 24h prefetch A/B with soft-warm, upload CSVs, deploy async metadata-write patch to staging and run load test; Maya will send pricing & SOC2 excerpt; Jordan/Ethan will instrument tail traces and share normalized prompts.
[10:27] Priya: one question on timeline - when can we expect a recommended production config if tests look good?
[10:33] Samir: if the 24h run is clean and patch reduces writes, i think 2 weeks to recommended prod knobs including TTLs and cohort sizing. so around 2026-09-02.
[10:44] Maya: great. scheduling follow-up: 2026-08-26 15:00 UTC. anything else?
[10:50] Jordan: none from me.
[10:51] Ethan: n/a.
[10:52] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]
